title: Hemocytometer (Counting Chamber)

references.label: General cell biology/microbiology laboratory manuals (ASM curriculum resources)

purpose: A thick glass slide etched with a precise grid of known area and chamber depth, used with a light microscope to manually count cells (or other particles) in a defined volume of suspension in order to calculate concentration.
operatingPrinciple: A coverslip rests on raised supports a fixed, known distance above the etched grid, creating a chamber of precisely known volume over each grid square; counting the cells within a defined set of grid squares and applying the chamber's known volume and any dilution factor yields the original sample's cell concentration.
basicOperation: Clean the hemocytometer and coverslip thoroughly before use.
Mount the coverslip on the raised supports so that Newton's rings (interference patterns) are visible, confirming correct, even seating.
Load a small volume of the (often stained, e.g. with trypan blue) cell suspension into the loading channel by capillary action, avoiding overfilling or underfilling the chamber.

Count cells within the designated grid squares under the microscope using a consistent counting rule (e.g. counting cells touching two specific sides of each square and excluding the other two) to avoid double-counting cells on grid lines.
Apply the chamber's known volume and any dilution factor to calculate the original concentration.
importantSettings: Consistent grid-square counting rule (which boundary cells are included) to avoid systematic over- or under-counting
calibration: The chamber's etched dimensions are fixed by manufacture; periodic inspection for scratches or damage to the grid substitutes for a calibration check.
maintenance: Clean immediately after use to prevent dried sample residue from affecting future counts.
Handle and store to avoid scratching the etched counting grid.

commonErrors.cause: Overfilled/underfilled chamber, uneven coverslip seating, or inconsistent boundary-cell counting rule between counts
commonErrors.fix: Reload with correct volume, confirm Newton's rings are visible, and apply the same boundary-counting rule every time

commonErrors.problem: Too few or too many cells per square to count reliably
commonErrors.cause: Sample too concentrated or too dilute for the chamber's practical counting range
commonErrors.fix: Adjust the dilution before loading so cell density falls within the range that is practical to count accurately

safety: Handle any biological sample per its risk assessment; dispose of used coverslips/loading material per biohazard waste procedures where applicable.
